question.text: Under the SEBI online ODR framework described on pages 239-240 of the NISM Series-VII (January 2026) workbook, in a dispute involving an individual investor, the venue and seat of the online ODR proceedings is deemed to be:

answer.text: The place where the individual investor resides permanently (as per KYC documents)
The location of the Market Participant's registered head office
Mumbai, in all online ODR proceedings, irrespective of the investor's location
New Delhi, in all online ODR proceedings, irrespective of the investor's location

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 239-240 of NISM Series-VII (January 2026) provide that, for an individual investor, the venue and seat of the online ODR proceedings is deemed to be the place where the investor resides permanently (per KYC documents). For non-individual / institutional / corporate clients, separate rules apply based on place of registration or principal place of business. The stem is now restricted to the individual-investor case, so the keyed option is uniquely correct. The Trap: The Market Participant's head office, Mumbai, and New Delhi are not the deemed venue under the workbook's rules for individual investors. The audit flagged the original because the unqualified "online ODR proceedings" stem ignored the separate institutional/corporate venue rules also described on pp.239-240, meaning the keyed option was not universal. Note: The original was ambiguous because pp.239-240 lay down multiple venue rules - individual investor residence, non-individual registration, and principal place of business / institutional alternatives. The stem is now qualified to a dispute involving an individual investor, which uniquely supports the "investor's permanent residence per KYC" answer.
